title: Introduce domain-level state mutation tools
description:
Keep low-level mutateState as an internal primitive, but stop making the model primarily reason in terms of storage columns and table fields.

Introduce higher-level domain operations for common canon-changing actions such as adjusting HP, adding/removing conditions, inventory changes, clock updates, plot flags, and world facts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Low-level mutateState remains available internally.
- Model-facing tools or descriptors prefer domain actions over persistence-column fields.
- Common operations have typed/domain-specific validation.
- Existing state mutation tests are preserved or migrated.
- Prompt/tool docs are updated to reflect the domain-level mutation path.
close_reason: Replaced single mutate_state model-facing tool with 8 domain tools (adjust_hp, add/remove_condition, give/remove_item, update_clock, set_plot_flag, set_world_fact). Low-level mutateState stays internal. 23 new domain mutation tests + all existing tests pass. Verification: typecheck, test (564 pass), check all exit 0.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: Verification: npm run typecheck -> exit 0; npm run test -> 564 passed, 3 skipped; npm run check -> exit 0, no fixes. All 5 acceptance criteria verified: mutateState internal, 8 domain tools in registry, typed validation (HP clamp, condition array ops, inventory qty), gameState.test.ts 7/7 pass unchanged, protocol prompt updated.
